about: Albert's calls for the Frankenstein Refresh, in order: the one home for them. Everything sorted or built in the refresh follows these.
calls: build and train times: Mid's. Every building's health: v100's (Age of Empires II's; walls that hold)
damage: open, to review in play; units' health open with it
soldiers: Shell Unit; its attributes (Age, Class, Level/evolution, Behavior, Attitude, Sprite, Motion, Speed, Health...) are the output; every kind is the Unit shell with its settings
sounds: the wind's kept; the eclipse's killed
the Yard stays Tall for now (the volume row)
ages: Mid's names (Stone, Bronze, Classical, Medieval, Gunpowder, the hidden Enlightenment)
the rule: Mid's gameplay comes over as it is, with its values, unless it meets a call made for v100; only those meetings go to Albert
the chain: Mid, divide, clean, sort, modulate, map to ECS, rewrite cleanly into v100

what was held and Mid built (ruts, floods, fire from lightning, moon and sky, small map, labels, ripples, woods blocking sight, spoilage, ground ice, formations, theatrics) comes over: clean, lean and mean, clear and tight
vassals pay tribute; the tax idea is parked
speed: 3.4 mph is the base; research improves it; weather, ground and load change it, each mapped to its law
building-health research comes over, as a share on top of v100's health
no surplus selling for anyone: the idea and its code cut, parked
the computers' free mill and farm: killed (they win enough)
the outpost wagon is the war camp's wagon, in two sizes: small, and large, which holds an army like a wall, a safe zone
the backup save stays; v100 starts fresh
Mid's menus are redesigned to fit v100's menus
research stacks and its percents add, applied once to the base: 3.0 with +10% and +8% is 3.0 × 1.18 = 3.54, not 3.0 × 1.10 × 1.08 = 3.564
yes yes: builds F10 to F39, in order, each through the gate and its match test; stop only for what doesn't fit; previews after F17, F25 and F37

the permit's cap of ten is lifted for the refresh: one build carries a whole module (or a few small ones), never split; the byte budget with its why, the gate and the match test hold every build; from F13b on
F14's three crowd rules, not Mid's, approved: keep right when meeting head-on; a walker pushed within a pace of its target has arrived; a villager is at a building within its ring plus a pace
whatever is cleaner, more effective and efficient; if it is not a problem, no change: the Measurements book stays one book
the tests: one shared loader for Mid's frozen code, a build runs only the tests its permit touches, the full set at publish; done as a tools build after F15
the Palisade comes only with the war camp, as in Mid (free there); it leaves the Walls tab
pace goes by the floor (ground), the weather, mass and gravity; never by the season or the calendar
the effects law: boosts add, applied once; cuts apply one at a time, each on what is left; never zero and never 100%; simpler, and it should cut code

weather is one system with an intensity, its strength from the randomizer: a blizzard is the top of it, by the governing body's definition (the US National Weather Service: wind 35 mph or more, visibility under a quarter mile, for 3 hours or more); nature and math first, an equation over a made-up number, an accepted definition over our own; as real as we are able
grip by math and physics: the friction the ground and the foot or hoof give against the friction the gait needs, from measured values with sources
crampons: they help walkers on foot and the engines' haulers; horses wait for horseshoes
weather has visuals, run and made by code and math (SoRen's approach, already the root of Mid's weather on the glass): wind shows in what it moves; no flat weather
you start in the corner drawn at the bottom left of the screen, whatever the view's turn
the pocket (Z1) and the corner hold resources: the calculated one age up (DICTIONARY Z1)

Z3 is a transition zone, laid by the Randomizer: a larger share of open, buildable space than Z4 so towns can build out, trees thickening toward Z4, resources in it (more than the pocket, less than the wilds)

rigid: zero stray numbers; every value lives in its designated book with its citation and its comment, with a rhyme or reason. Every piece is checked against the core values, in order: Is it fair? Does it follow our logic and rules? Is there a real-life solution? Real-life math? Science? Purpose? Function? One home? The typed numbers left in code are swept into their books after F39, module by module, the gate's ratchet lowered as each empties
the civilisations: as Mid had them, if they come clean and within our rules
the Games wait with the Throne
scale: shrink the person to scale rather than shorten the buildings (the board is too small anyway; later)
trees: real heights by kind and age, from the USDA Forest Service (or the governing forestry source)
